In today’s News and Commentary, the Trump administration prepares to roll back pregnancy-related job protections, a federal court ruling favors an AI whistleblower, and voter enthusiasm among union members soars ahead of Election Day.

According to insiders, the Trump administration is planning to reduce the scope of regulations under the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA). Passed in 2022, the PWFA was meant to address a meaningful gap in disability and discrimination protection for pregnant workers. Then, in 2024, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) under the Biden administration adopted a broad reading of the PWFA’s text, resulting in many more pregnancy-related conditions and procedures being covered by the statute. However, Andrea Lucas, the current EEOC Chair, has been vocal in her disagreement with the 2024 rule and supports a narrower reading of the statute. Lucas’s proposed approach would eliminate coverage for a number of procedures, including IVF and other fertility treatments. The EEOC has not made an official comment on possible regulatory changes, but commentators expect litigation to ensue if these changes are made. For more details on the potential ramifications of a new EEOC ruling, check out Mia’s piece here.

On Monday, the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit sided with an AI whistleblower by lowering the evidentiary threshold required to obtain a hearing before a Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) administrative judge.
